items.title: fix: preserve approval sandbox decisions in unified exec

observed_change: Codex preserves approved sandbox-escalation decisions through unified-exec launch and intercepted shell exec paths while keeping bounded additional-permission requests sandboxed.
evidence: The upstream review records explicit divergent handling for `UseDefault`, `RequireEscalated`, and `WithAdditionalPermissions`.
The PR body says denied-read profiles and bounded additional-permission requests must remain sandboxed.
Unified exec launch setup now derives `launch_sandbox_permissions` before managed-network, environment, and launch sandbox selection.
New zsh-fork unified-exec tests cover parent approval preservation, policy bypass, bounded additional permissions, denied-read preservation, and managed-network environment stripping.
candidate_followups: Audit Decodex sandbox and approval summaries for any wording that collapses additional permissions into full escalation.
Use the upstream fix as a compatibility note when explaining unified-exec approval behavior in release rollups.
Watch for follow-up upstream changes in the stacked PR #24982 mentioned by the PR footer.
social_notes: Public copy should frame this as precise sandbox/approval behavior, not as broader permission expansion.
caveats: The change is a correctness fix for approved and policy-allowed execution paths.
No new user-facing flag or command is introduced by the PR.
